problems.title: Recover the number of black balls
problems.question: A box has 22 balls. Drawing two without replacement has probability $12/77$ of both black. How many are black?
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
steps: Set the probability equal to $12/77$: $b(b-1)=72$.
$(b-9)(b+8)=0$, so the positive count is 9.

problems.title: Seven independent misses
problems.question: A shooter hits with probability $9/10$. Find the probability of missing on all seven independent shots.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
formulas: Miss probability is $1/10$; independent probabilities multiply.
steps: The probability is $(1/10)^7=10^{-7}$.

problems.title: A uniformly selected two-digit square
problems.question: Find the probability that a uniformly chosen two-digit natural number is a perfect square.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
steps: The squares are $16,25,36,49,64,81$, six values.
The probability is $6/90=1/15$.

problems.title: Equal lengths of a vector sum and difference
problems.question: Nonzero vectors $a,b$ satisfy $|a+b|=|a-b|$. What follows about their angle?
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
steps: Equating the squares gives $4a\cdot b=0$, so $a\cdot b=0$.
Nonzero vectors with zero dot product are perpendicular.

problems.title: Area from a two-by-two determinant
problems.question: Find the parallelogram area generated by $(1,2)$ and $(3,1)$.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.

problems.title: One die result divides the other
problems.question: Two fair independent dice are rolled. Find the probability that one outcome divides the other.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
formulas: Count ordered pairs among 36 equally likely outcomes.
steps: With the smaller value first, divisibility gives $6+3+2+1+1+1=14$ pairs. Six of these are equal pairs; the other eight have two orderings.
Therefore there are $6+2(8)=22$ favourable ordered outcomes, giving $22/36=11/18$.

problems.title: One result of one kind in three biased tosses
problems.question: A coin has probabilities $1/3$ for one face and $2/3$ for the other. Find the probability of exactly one first-face result in three independent tosses.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
formulas: There are $\binom31=3$ possible positions for the first-face result.
steps: Each ordering has probability $(1/3)(2/3)^2=4/27$. Add the three disjoint orderings to get $4/9$.

problems.title: A random triangle in an isosceles trapezoid
problems.question: $AB=BC=CD$ and $A=D=60^\circ$. Choose $K$ uniformly on larger base $AD$. Find the probability that $BCK$ is acute.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
formulas: A triangle angle is acute iff the dot product of its two rays is positive.
steps: Scale the equal lengths to 1. Use $A=(0,0),D=(2,0),B=(1/2,\sqrt3/2),C=(3/2,\sqrt3/2)$ and $K=(x,0)$.
The angles at $B,C$ are acute precisely when $x>1/2$ and $x<3/2$. The dot product at $K$ is $(x-1)^2+1/2>0$, so its angle is always acute.
The favourable interval has length 1 out of the base length 2.

problems.title: Length of a vector difference
problems.question: $|a|=\sqrt3,|b|=2$, and their angle is $30^\circ$. Find $|3a-2b|$.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
steps: $a\cdot b=\sqrt3\cdot2\cos30^\circ=3$. Hence the squared length is $27+16-36=7$.

problems.title: Incircle of a coordinate right triangle
problems.question: $A=(1,1),B=(9,7),C=(1,7)$. Find the incircle equation.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
steps: The legs are 6 and 8 and hypotenuse 10, so $r=2$. Starting from right vertex $C=(1,7)$, move 2 units toward the interior in each coordinate direction to get centre $(3,5)$.

problems.title: A random parameter and a root statistic
problems.question: Choose $k$ uniformly in $[1,10]$. Find the probability that roots of $x^2-5kx+6k^2=0$ have squared sum at most 52.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
steps: The squared sum is $4k^2+9k^2=13k^2\le52$, so $|k|\le2$.
Within the given interval this is $[1,2]$, length 1 out of total length 9.

problems.title: Largest possible mean with median, mode and range fixed
problems.question: Four natural numbers have unique mode 3, median 3 and range 3. Find the largest possible mean.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
formulas: For sorted data $w\le x\le y\le z$, median is $(x+y)/2$.
steps: The repeated mode 3 must occupy the two middle positions, so $x=y=3$. Otherwise, if the two middle values straddled 3, there would be no place for repeated 3s.
Range 3 gives $z=w+3$, and $w\le3$. The total is $w+3+3+(w+3)=2w+9$, maximized at $w=3$.
The data $3,3,3,6$ meet all conditions, with mean $15/4$.

problems.title: Standard deviation of four values
problems.question: Find the population standard deviation of $1,2,2,3$.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
steps: The mean is 2. Squared deviations are $1,0,0,1$, whose average is $1/2$.
Thus the standard deviation is $\sqrt{1/2}=\sqrt2/2$.

problems.title: A circle tangent to a given line
problems.question: Which circle centred at $(1,2)$ among the choices is tangent to $2x+3y+5=0$?
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
formulas: Tangency requires radius equal to centre-to-line distance.
steps: The distance is $|2+6+5|/\sqrt{2^2+3^2}=13/\sqrt{13}=\sqrt{13}$.
Thus the squared radius must be 13.

problems.title: Two intersections between a line and a unit circle
problems.question: For which $a$ does $y=x+a$ meet $x^2+y^2=1$ at two distinct points?
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
formulas: A line cuts a circle twice iff its distance from the centre is less than the radius.
steps: The distance from the origin to $x-y+a=0$ is $|a|/\sqrt2$. Require $|a|/\sqrt2<1$.

problems.title: Equal sums of successive triples
problems.question: $a_{100}=100,a_{200}=200,a_{300}=300$, and every three consecutive terms have the same sum. Find $a_{10}+a_{20}+a_{30}$.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
formulas: Subtract consecutive triple-sum identities to obtain $a_{n+3}=a_n$.
steps: The sequence has period 3. Indices 10 and 100 share remainder 1; 20 and 200 share remainder 2; 30 and 300 share remainder 0.
The requested sum is therefore $100+200+300=600$.

problems.title: An infinite decimal geometric series
problems.question: Evaluate $0.9+0.09+0.009+\cdots$.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
steps: The first term is 0.9 and ratio 0.1, so $S=0.9/0.9=1$.

problems.title: Four years of compound growth
problems.question: A bacterial population starts at $10^4$ and grows by 10% each year. Find the population after four years in this model.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.

problems.title: Angle between two lines inside a square
problems.question: A square has side 4. $M$ is the midpoint of $CD$; $K\in BC$ with $BK:KC=3:1$. Find the cosine between lines $AK,BM$.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
formulas: The smaller line-angle cosine is $|u\cdot v|/(|u||v|)$.
steps: The absolute dot product is 4; lengths are 5 and $2\sqrt5$. The cosine is $2/(5\sqrt5)$.

problems.title: Distance of a line intersection from a square side
problems.question: Use the same side-4 square, midpoint $M\in CD$ and $BK:KC=3:1$. Find the distance from $AK\cap BM$ to side $AB$.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
formulas: In coordinates, distance to the horizontal line $AB$ is the absolute ordinate.
steps: $AK$ is $y=3x/4$; $BM$ is $y=8-2x$. Equate to get $x=32/11$, $y=24/11$.
The perpendicular foot is on segment $AB$ since $0<32/11<4$. Thus the distance to the side is $24/11$.

problems.title: Sum of the first odd numbers
problems.question: Fill the statement: “The ___ of the first $n$ ___ natural numbers equals $n^2$.”
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
steps: The arithmetic-series sum simplifies to $n^2$. Thus the words are “sum” and “odd.”
problems.answer: The sum of the first $n$ odd natural numbers is $n^2$.

problems.title: Count positive arithmetic terms
problems.question: How many positive terms occur in $20.3,18.7,17.1,\ldots$?
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
steps: Positivity gives $n<1+20.3/1.6=13.6875$. The positive indices are 1 through 13.

problems.title: Partial sums determine a later partial sum
problems.question: An arithmetic progression has $S_{10}=20$ and $S_{20}=20$. Find $S_{30}$.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
steps: The equations are $100A+10B=20$ and $400A+20B=20$. Subtract twice the first to get $200A=-20$, so $A=-1/10$ and $B=3$.

problems.title: Which segments cross a line?
problems.question: $A=(1,1),B=(2,1),C=(1,2)$. Which segments $AB,AC,BC$ cross $2x-5y+4=0$?
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
formulas: A linear expression changes sign along a segment iff that segment crosses its zero line, provided neither endpoint is on it.
steps: The expression values at $A,B,C$ are $1,3,-4$.
$AC$ and $BC$ have endpoints with opposite signs, so both cross the line. $AB$ stays on its positive side.

problems.title: Triangle area with a vertical base
problems.question: Find the area of the triangle with $A=(0,7),B=(0,1),C=(4,0)$.
problems.idea: Apply the definition or formula, keeping the assumptions explicit.
steps: Base $AB$ is vertical with length 6; the perpendicular distance from $C$ to its line is 4.
The area is $6\cdot4/2=12$.
